correctness.rationale: Passes the corrected statement in repairs/4, not the original identification with the totient–divisor equation. For P−2F=5 the normalized Euler product 2F/P is less than one. If p≥5 the product is at least 5760/5005>1; with p=3, q≥11 would give at least 4000/3993>1. Thus q=5 or 7. For q=7 the whole left side P−2F is divisible by 3. For q=5 the reduction is (r−16)(s−16)=235. Negative factors give product at most 45 and the two positive pairs give (17,251) and (21,63), only the first prime. Substituting gives P=64005, F=32000. An independent solved-for-s check over r≤31 (from the positive ordered factors of 235) found the same survivor; the exact algebra, not this finite check alone, exhausts the original unbounded domain. With m=16P, phi(4m)=32F and d(4m)=(6+1)·16, so the actual condition is P−2F=7 and at the stated tuple the sum is 1024112, not m=1024080. The final repair retains only uniqueness for the displayed equation as its contribution; it documents the normalization error and cites the existing obstruction for the actual equation. The replacement verifier was independently written and run; its output matches repairs/4/verification_output.txt.
